In Fort Kochi an old man who mended the great fishing nets on the shore was teaching his grandson. The boy asked why the net did not tear when it was full. The old man showed him the knots: each one small, each one tied by hand, each one holding its neighbour. One knot alone holds nothing, he said, but a thousand knots together can lift the sea. Then he added: that is why we go to Mass together on Sunday. The Lord fills the net, and we hold one another.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen and standing on the shore of our lives, call to us, fill our nets and feed us with your bread. Alleluia. Amen.
share: By what power or by what name did you do this? (Acts 4:7). What would I answer if someone asked me why I live as I do?
That night they caught nothing (John 21:3). Where have I been working without the Lord?
Come and have breakfast (John 21:12). How do I answer the Lord's invitation to the Eucharist?
pm.resp: The stone rejected by the builders has become the cornerstone.
interc: For the Pope and the bishops, successors of Peter and the Apostles, that they may speak the name of Jesus with courage.
For all who seek God with a sincere heart, that they may come to know Christ the Saviour.
For fishermen and all who labour through the night, especially on the coasts of Kerala.
For families devoted to the Sacred Heart on this First Friday.
For our group, that we may recognize the Lord and say with joy: It is the Lord!
pm.close: Father, the stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. Build us up on Christ, and make us one in the net of your Church. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The council saw the boldness of Peter and John and knew they had been with Jesus.
“We cannot keep from speaking about what we have seen and heard.”
The Risen Lord rebuked the Eleven for their unbelief, then sent them into all the world.
2027-04-03.action: Finish the Divine Mercy Novena today, and go to confession if you can before tomorrow.
2027-04-03.question: Would anyone who watched me this week guess that I have been with Jesus?
catechism: The doubts of the disciples and the reality of the Resurrection.
kidsaint: St Richard of Chichester

Richard was a bishop in England who loved the poor. He gave away so much that his helpers worried there would be nothing left! He wrote a little prayer: dear Jesus, help me to know you more clearly, love you more dearly and follow you more nearly, day by day. Lesson: we can pray Richard's prayer every morning.
2027-04-03.special: Saturday within the Octave of Easter (solemnity): Gloria; the Easter Sequence may be sung; double Alleluia at the dismissal. First Saturday of the month.
term: Parrēsia (boldness)
A Greek word for freedom and courage in speaking, especially speaking the truth before the powerful. In Acts it is a gift of the Holy Spirit to the Apostles and to all who witness to Jesus.

family.explain: The leaders told Peter and John: stop talking about Jesus! But Peter and John said: we cannot stop speaking about what we have seen and heard. They had seen Jesus alive, and they were so happy that they had to tell everyone.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who are not allowed to speak about Jesus, that God may give them courage and keep them safe.
family.ask: Ask: “What is the best thing we know about Jesus?” Choose together one person to tell this week.

illus: An illustration

A young clerk in a bank in Thrissur was told by his manager to change a date on a loan record so that a powerful customer could avoid a penalty. He said politely that he could not do it. The manager was angry, and within months the clerk was transferred to a small branch far from home. Two years later an audit found the old irregularities, and the manager was removed. The clerk's mother said only: you obeyed God, and he did not forget you. It is a small story, but it is the same answer Peter gave: whether it is right to listen to you rather than to God, you must judge.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen from the dead, let us be with you now, and fill us with the boldness of your Holy Spirit. Alleluia. Amen.
share: They recognized them as companions of Jesus (Acts 4:13). What in my life shows that I have been with Jesus?
We cannot keep from speaking about what we have seen and heard (Acts 4:20). What have I seen and heard of God that I keep to myself?
Go into all the world (Mark 16:15). Where is my little part of the world?
pm.resp: I praise you, Lord, for you have answered me.
interc: For Christians who suffer for their faith, that they may have the courage of Peter and John.
For those in authority, that they may never command what is against God's law.
For all who are slow to believe, that the Risen Lord may be patient with them as with the Eleven.
For the newly baptized of this Easter, that they may keep the white garment of grace unstained.
For our group, that we may finish the Divine Mercy Novena with faith and prepare well for tomorrow.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son's disciples into all the world. Make us faithful companions of Jesus and joyful messengers of his good news. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Annunciation is moved to today because 25 March was Holy Thursday.
The Son said to the Father: a body you have prepared for me; see, I have come to do your will.
Mary said: here am I, the servant of the Lord; and the Word became flesh in her womb.
2027-04-05.action: At Mass today kneel at the words “and became man”; at noon pray the Regina Caeli as a family.
2027-04-05.question: What is God asking of me now, and am I answering like Ahaz or like Mary?
catechism: The Annunciation inaugurates the fullness of time.
Mary's yes: the obedience of faith.
The Incarnation: the Son of God assumed a human nature.
kidsaint: Our Lady at Nazareth

Mary was a young girl in a small village. One day the angel Gabriel came and said: God has chosen you to be the mother of his Son. Mary was surprised, but she loved God, so she said: yes, let it happen as you say. And Jesus began to grow inside her. Lesson: when God asks something, we can say yes like Mary.
2027-04-05.special: Solemnity of the Annunciation of the Lord, transferred from 25 March. White vestments, Gloria and Creed; all genuflect at “and became man.” Alleluia is added because it is Eastertide.
term: Incarnation

From the Latin for “becoming flesh”: the mystery that the eternal Son of God took a full human nature, body and soul, in the womb of the Virgin Mary by the power of the Holy Spirit, without ceasing to be God (John 1:14; Catechism 461–463). It began at the Annunciation.

family.explain: God sent the angel Gabriel to a girl called Mary in a small town called Nazareth. The angel said: you will have a baby, and he will be the Son of God, and his name will be Jesus. Mary asked how, and the angel said: the Holy Spirit will do it; nothing is impossible for God. Mary said: I am God's servant; let it be as you say.
family.intention: We pray for all mothers who are expecting a baby, and for every child not yet born.
family.ask: Ask: “What does it mean to say yes to God?” Then pray the Hail Mary together slowly, stopping at each line.

illus: An illustration

A young mother in a fishing village near Kollam was told in the fifth month that her baby would be born with a serious heart condition. Relatives advised her quietly to end the pregnancy. Each night she sat with her rosary and stopped at the first Joyful Mystery. Later she told her parish priest: I kept hearing one sentence, nothing will be impossible with God, and I said to Mary, I do not know how, but let it be. The child needed two operations and is now in school. She did not choose the easy road; she chose the yes.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, who overshadowed the Virgin Mary, come upon us as we pray. Make us listen as she listened. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Ask a sign of the Lord your God (Isaiah 7:11). Where have I, like Ahaz, refused God's help out of fear?
See, God, I have come to do your will (Hebrews 10:7). How does Jesus' own yes to the Father change the way I pray?
Here am I, the servant of the Lord (Luke 1:38). What yes is God asking of me this Easter?
pm.resp: Here I am, Lord; I come to do your will.
interc: For the Church, that like Mary she may welcome the Word and give Christ to the world.
For expecting mothers, especially those afraid or alone, and for every unborn child.
For young people discerning their vocation, that they may hear the angel's “Do not be afraid.”
For all who find it hard to trust God, that nothing may seem impossible to them with God.
For our group, that we may keep the Word in our hearts and bring him to others.
pm.close: Father, your Word became flesh in the womb of the Virgin Mary. By her prayers make us servants of your will and witnesses of your risen Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The first Christians were of one heart and soul and shared what they had, so that no one was in need.
Barnabas, the son of encouragement, sold his field and gave the money to the apostles.
Jesus told Nicodemus: as Moses lifted up the serpent, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, so that believers may have eternal life.
2027-04-06.action: Put aside something today, money, food or time, for a family in need in your parish.
2027-04-06.question: What do I hold on to as if Christ had not risen?

family.explain: After Jesus rose from the dead, his friends loved each other so much that they shared everything. Nobody was hungry and nobody was left out. A man called Barnabas even sold his field and gave the money to help the poor.
family.intention: We pray for families who do not have enough food or a home.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share this week?” Choose one thing together and do it.

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Alappuzha the youth group noticed that the same three families never came to the parish feast meal, because they could not pay the contribution. That Easter the young people quietly asked every household to put one handful of rice aside each day in a special tin. At the end of the Octave they had enough for the three families for two months. They called it the Barnabas tin. Nobody was told whose rice was whose.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, wind of God, blow through our hearts and make us one heart and one soul. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Everything they owned was held in common (Acts 4:32). What does my use of money say about my faith in the Resurrection?
Barnabas, which means son of encouragement (Acts 4:36). Who has been a Barnabas to me, and to whom can I be one?
So must the Son of Man be lifted up (John 3:14). What do I need to bring to the cross to be healed?
pm.resp: The Lord is king; he is robed in majesty.
interc: For the Church, that she may be one heart and soul, and that there may be no one in need among us.
For the poor of our parish and village, that they may find brothers and sisters in us.
For all who are discouraged, that God may send them a Barnabas.
For those seeking God in the dark like Nicodemus, that the Spirit may bring them to the light.
For our group, that we may look to the Crucified and Risen One and live.
pm.close: Father, your Son was lifted up so that all who believe may have life. Make us one in heart and generous in love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: An angel opened the prison doors at night and sent the apostles back to preach in the Temple.
God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, not to condemn the world but to save it.
St John Baptist de la Salle gave his fortune and his life to teaching poor children; he is the patron of teachers.
2027-04-07.action: Pray today for one teacher by name, and thank one teacher in person or by message.
2027-04-07.question: Do I come to the light, or do I hide some part of my life from God?
kidsaint: St John Baptist de la Salle

John was a rich young priest in France. He saw many poor children who could not go to school. He gave away his money, gathered good teachers and opened schools for them without fees. He taught them about reading and writing, and most of all about Jesus. Lesson: helping others learn is a way of loving them.

family.explain: Jesus said: God loves the whole world so much that he gave us his only Son. He did not send Jesus to punish the world, but to save it. Whoever believes in Jesus will live for ever with God.
family.intention: We pray for all our teachers, and for children who cannot go to school.
family.ask: Ask: “Which teacher helped you the most, and why?” Then say a Hail Mary for that teacher.

illus: An illustration

In a government school in Palakkad district, a teacher noticed a boy who sat at the back and never opened his notebook. Instead of scolding him, she stayed back one evening and asked him to read a single line. He could not. His father worked in a quarry and nobody at home could read. She spent twenty minutes with him every evening for a year. Years later he became a primary-school teacher himself, and on his first day he went looking for the child at the back of the class.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the world, open the doors of our hearts and send us out with your message of life. Alleluia. Amen.
share: An angel of the Lord opened the prison doors (Acts 5:19). What prison of fear or habit do I need the Lord to open?
God did not send the Son into the world to condemn the world (John 3:17). Do I think of God more as judge or as Saviour?
Those who do what is true come to the light (John 3:21). What in my life needs to come into the light?
pm.resp: The Lord hears the cry of the poor.
interc: For teachers, catechists and all who form the young, through the prayers of St John Baptist de la Salle.
For children who cannot go to school because of poverty, work or war.
For Christians imprisoned for their faith, that the Lord may strengthen and release them.
For those who live in darkness, that they may come to the light of Christ.
For our group, that we may tell the whole message of this life.
pm.close: Father, you so loved the world that you gave your Son. Make us teachers of his love by word and example. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Before the council the apostles said: we must obey God rather than any human authority.
Peter preached that God raised Jesus to give repentance and forgiveness of sins.
Jesus speaks the words of God and gives the Spirit without measure; the Father has placed all things in his hands.
2027-04-08.action: Pray “Come, Holy Spirit” once this morning and once this evening, asking for courage to witness.
2027-04-08.question: Is there a place in my life where I keep quiet about Jesus because I fear what others will think?

family.explain: The leaders told the apostles: stop talking about Jesus! But Peter said: we must obey God first. God raised Jesus from the dead, and we have seen him. The Holy Spirit makes us brave to tell everyone.
family.intention: We pray for Christians in countries where it is dangerous to speak about Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard to do what God wants, and who can help us?”

illus: An illustration

A young accountant in a firm in Kochi was asked by his manager to change some figures before an audit. He was newly married and could not afford to lose his job. He asked for one night to think, prayed in front of the Blessed Sacrament at a city church, and the next morning told his manager respectfully that he could not do it. The manager was angry, but the audit found the original figures correct. Two years later, when the firm was investigated, his name was the only one nobody questioned.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, given without measure, fill us with courage and with love, and make us witnesses of the risen Lord. Alleluia. Amen.
share: We must obey God rather than any human authority (Acts 5:29). Where do I face a choice like this?
That he might give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins (Acts 5:31). Do I carry Easter as a message of forgiveness or of blame?
He gives the Spirit without measure (John 3:34). Do I ask for the Spirit generously or timidly?
pm.resp: The Lord hears the cry of the poor.
interc: For Christians under pressure to deny their faith, that the Spirit may give them courage.
For all in authority, that they may respect conscience and serve the truth.
For friendship and respect between Christians and the Jewish people.
For those who must choose between their job and their conscience.
For our group, that we may be witnesses together with the Holy Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you have placed all things in your Son's hands. Give us his Spirit and make us faithful witnesses. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Gamaliel told the council: if this work is of God, you cannot overthrow it.
The apostles were flogged and rejoiced to suffer for the name of Jesus.
Jesus fed five thousand people with five barley loaves and two fish, and twelve baskets were left over.
2027-04-09.action: Give the value of one meal today to a poor family or to the parish charity box.
2027-04-09.question: What is my “five loaves,” and have I placed it in Jesus' hands?

family.explain: A huge crowd was hungry. A boy had only five small loaves and two fish. He gave them to Jesus. Jesus thanked God, and shared them, and everyone ate as much as they wanted! There were twelve baskets left over.
family.intention: We pray for children who go to sleep hungry tonight.
family.ask: Ask: “What small thing can I give Jesus today?” Each one names something, and the family helps them do it.

illus: An illustration

In a hill parish in Idukki the Sunday school children decided during Lent to bring one coin each week for a boy in their class whose father had died. By Easter the tin held barely enough for a pair of school shoes. A shopkeeper in town heard the story, added the rest of the uniform and a year's books, and told the parish priest: I could not let those children's coins be wasted. Five loaves become twelve baskets when someone gives first.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Bread of Life, we bring you our little loaves; bless them, break them and share them. Alleluia. Amen.
share: If it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow them (Acts 5:39). Do I trust that God's work will last even when it looks weak?
They rejoiced that they were considered worthy to suffer dishonor for the sake of the name (Acts 5:41). How do I bear insult for my faith?
There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish (John 6:9). What small gift is the Lord asking from me?
pm.resp: One thing I seek: to dwell in the house of the Lord.
interc: For the Church, that she may feed the hungry with bread and with the Word.
For Christians who suffer insult or violence for the name of Jesus, that they may know Easter joy.
For leaders and judges, that they may have the wisdom and justice of Gamaliel.
For the hungry of our village and our world, and for an end to the waste of food.
For our group, that we may give Jesus what little we have.
pm.close: Father, your Son fed the multitude and gives himself as the Bread of Life. Make us generous and grateful. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Greek-speaking widows were being neglected, and the apostles listened to the complaint.
Seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom were chosen to serve, and the apostles laid hands on them.
Jesus came walking on the stormy sea and said: It is I; do not be afraid.
2027-04-10.action: Visit, call or help one widow or elderly person living alone this weekend.
2027-04-10.question: Who in my parish or family is being quietly forgotten?

family.explain: The disciples were in a boat at night. The wind was strong, the waves were big, and they were scared. Then they saw Jesus walking on the water! He said: It is I; do not be afraid. As soon as they took him into the boat, they reached the shore.
family.intention: We pray for fishermen at sea tonight, and for all who are afraid.
family.ask: Ask: “What makes us afraid?” Then each one says: Jesus, it is you; I will not be afraid.

illus: An illustration

A group of fishermen from Vizhinjam were caught in a sudden squall far from the coast one monsoon night. The engine failed and the radio went dead. The oldest of them, who had led the rosary at the harbour chapel for thirty years, made them all hold on to the boat and pray together, aloud, again and again: Jesus, it is you; do not let us be afraid. At dawn a coast guard vessel found them, drifting but alive. Back on shore, he said: the sea did not become calm at once, but we did.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, who walk on the waters, come to us in our storms and speak your word: It is I; do not be afraid. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Their widows were being neglected (Acts 6:1). Whom do I overlook without meaning to?
We will devote ourselves to prayer and to serving the word (Acts 6:4). How can I support my priests and deacons in their ministry?
It was now dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them (John 6:17). Where in my life is it dark and Jesus seems absent?
pm.resp: Lord, let your mercy be on us, as we place our trust in you.
interc: For deacons, priests and bishops, that they may be full of the Spirit and of wisdom.
For widows, the elderly and all who are neglected, that the Church may never forget them.
For communities divided by language or culture, that they may become one family.
For fishermen and all who travel by sea, and for all who are afraid.
For our group, that in every storm we may hear Jesus say: It is I.
pm.close: Father, your Son walks on the stormy sea and brings us safe to shore. Keep us trusting in his presence. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Stephen, full of grace and the Spirit, was falsely accused, and his face shone like an angel's.
The crowd looked for Jesus because they had eaten bread, not because they had understood the sign.
Jesus said: work for the food that endures; the work of God is to believe in the One he has sent.
2027-04-12.action: Spend ten quiet minutes today with John 6 or before the tabernacle.
2027-04-12.question: Do I come to Jesus mostly for what I want from him, or for him?

family.explain: After Jesus fed thousands of people with five loaves, the people went looking for him the next day. Jesus said: you are looking for me because you got bread to eat! But there is a better bread, one that lasts for ever, and I will give it to you. They asked: what must we do? Jesus said: believe in me.
family.intention: We pray for people who are hungry today, and for all who are hungry for God without knowing it.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing I usually ask Jesus for? Can I also tell him today that I love him, without asking anything?”

illus: An illustration

A woman in Alappuzha ran a small tea shop beside a bus stand. For years she served morning tea to the same drivers and conductors, and she always kept a small picture of the Sacred Heart above the stove. One driver, a rough young man, asked her mockingly why she wasted money on candles in front of a picture. She said: you come here for tea because it keeps you awake till noon. I go to him because he keeps me alive for ever. The young man laughed. Two years later, after an accident that nearly killed him, he came to the shop, sat down without ordering anything, and asked her which church she went to.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Bread of Life, we have come looking for you. Purify our hearts so that we seek you for your own sake. Alleluia. Amen.
share: They saw that his face was like the face of an angel (Acts 6:15). What gives a person that kind of peace under attack?
You are looking for me… because you ate your fill of the loaves (John 6:26). What do I mostly ask of Jesus?
This is the work of God, that you believe (John 6:29). How can my faith become my first work each day?
pm.resp: Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord! Alleluia.
interc: For Christians who are falsely accused or persecuted for their faith, that they may have Stephen's peace.
For deacons and all who serve the poor at the Church's tables.
For those who work hard only for the food that perishes, that they may find the bread that endures.
For the newly baptized of this Easter, that their faith may deepen week by week.
For our group, that we may seek Jesus for himself.
pm.close: Father, you set your seal on your Son and give him to us as the bread that endures. Make our faith strong and our faces bright with his peace. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Stephen saw heaven opened and Jesus standing at God's right hand; he died praying for his killers.
Saul, who would become St Paul, approved of his death.
Jesus said: I am the bread of life; the Father gives the true bread from heaven.
2027-04-13.action: Pray Stephen's prayer today for someone who has hurt you.
2027-04-13.question: Whom do I need to place in God's hands with the words: do not hold this sin against them?
kidsaint: St Martin I, pope

A pope who lived about 1,400 years ago. A powerful emperor wanted him to stop teaching the full truth about Jesus. Martin said no. Soldiers took him far away, to a cold place by the sea, where he did not even have enough bread. But he kept loving Jesus and praying for the Church until he died. Lesson: telling the truth about Jesus is worth more than being comfortable.

family.explain: Stephen loved Jesus so much that he would not stop speaking about him. Some angry men threw stones at him. But Stephen looked up and saw heaven open and Jesus standing there. He did not shout at the men. He prayed: Lord, do not hold this sin against them. That is just what Jesus did on the cross.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for Jesus today.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone I am angry with? Can we pray for them together tonight?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Kannur an old man was known for a quarrel with his brother that had lasted twenty years, over a strip of land and a coconut tree. When his brother died suddenly, he refused to go to the funeral. That night his grandson, preparing for his First Communion, read him the story of Stephen from his catechism book and asked: Appooppa, what does it mean, do not hold this sin against them? The old man did not answer. In the morning he was the first one at the cemetery, standing alone by the fresh grave, his lips moving.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, true bread from heaven, receive our spirits and teach us to forgive as Stephen forgave. Alleluia. Amen.
share: I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing (Acts 7:56). Where do I need to lift my eyes from my troubles to Jesus?
Lord, do not hold this sin against them (Acts 7:60). Is there anyone I am still holding a sin against?
Whoever comes to me will never be hungry (John 6:35). What hunger in me only Jesus can fill?
pm.resp: Into your hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. Alleluia.
interc: For persecuted Christians, that they may have Stephen's vision and forgiving heart.
For Pope and bishops, that like St Martin I they may guard the truth about Christ with courage.
For those who have hurt us, and for those whom we have hurt.
For prisoners and exiles, and for all who lack daily bread.
For our group, that we may come to Jesus and never be hungry.
pm.close: Father, you give us the true bread from heaven. Make us faithful witnesses to your Son, even when it costs us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: After Stephen's death the believers were scattered, and wherever they went they proclaimed the word.
Philip preached Christ in Samaria, and there was great joy in that city.
Jesus said: anyone who comes to me I will never drive away, and I will raise them up on the last day.
2027-04-14.action: Bring to Jesus today something you have been afraid to bring him.
2027-04-14.question: Where has God turned a scattering in my life into a sowing?

family.explain: Jesus said a beautiful thing: anyone who comes to me, I will never send away. Even if we have done something wrong, even if we feel small or sad, Jesus is always happy when we come to him. And he promised that on the last day he will raise us up, so that we live with him for ever.
family.intention: We pray for families who live far from home, especially our relatives working abroad.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family lives far away? Let us call or message them this week and pray for them by name.”

illus: An illustration

A nurse from Pala went to work in a hospital in a small German town where there was no Malayali family and no Mass in any language she knew. For the first months she cried after every night shift. Then she began to pray the rosary aloud in the hospital chapel at five in the morning. A Filipino cleaner joined her, then a Polish doctor, then a nurse from Kerala who had stopped practising her faith years before. When the parish priest found six people praying in three languages, he asked them to read at the Sunday Mass.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you drive no one away. We come to you just as we are. Fill us with the joy of Samaria. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Those who were scattered went from place to place, proclaiming the word (Acts 8:4). How can my difficulties become a way of spreading the Gospel?
So there was great joy in that city (Acts 8:8). Where have I seen the joy that Christ brings to a place?
Anyone who comes to me I will never drive away (John 6:37). Is there someone I keep at a distance whom Jesus would welcome?
pm.resp: Let all the earth cry out to God with joy. Alleluia.
interc: For Christians scattered by persecution or war, that they may carry the word wherever they go.
For Malayali migrants and all who work far from home, and for the families they support.
For deacons, catechists and missionaries who, like Philip, bring Christ to new places.
For those who think Jesus would turn them away, that they may come to him without fear.
For our beloved dead, that the Lord may raise them up on the last day.
pm.close: Father, your will is that none be lost. Keep us close to your Son, the bread of life, and bring us all to the resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: An angel sent Philip to a desert road, where an Ethiopian official was reading Isaiah.
Philip explained the passage about the Lamb and proclaimed Jesus; the man was baptized and went on his way rejoicing.
Jesus said: I am the living bread; the bread I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.
2027-04-15.action: Read and explain this Sunday's Gospel to someone younger in the faith.
2027-04-15.question: Do I let someone guide me in understanding Scripture, or do I read alone and give up?

family.explain: A rich man from far away Ethiopia was riding home in his chariot, reading the Bible, but he could not understand it. God sent Philip to run beside the chariot! Philip explained that the Bible was speaking about Jesus. The man believed, and when they saw some water he said: here is water, baptize me! He went home full of joy.
family.intention: We pray for people who want to know God but have no one to explain the faith to them.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught me about Jesus? Let us thank God for them tonight.”

illus: An illustration

A software engineer in Kochi, raised a Catholic but long uninterested, picked up his grandmother's Malayalam Bible after her funeral because it was full of her pencil marks. He could not make sense of most of it. One evening he asked the elderly sacristan, who was locking the church, what one underlined verse meant. The sacristan sat down on the steps and talked with him until it was dark. They met every Thursday after that. A year later the young man was reading at the Easter Vigil.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, living bread from heaven, draw us to yourself, open the Scriptures to us, and send us on our way rejoicing. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Do you understand what you are reading? How can I, unless someone guides me? (Acts 8:30–31). Who has been a Philip for me, and for whom can I be one?
Look, here is water! What is to prevent me from being baptized? (Acts 8:36). What do I think keeps people away from Christ, and is it real?
The bread that I will give for the life of the world is my flesh (John 6:51). How do I prepare to receive the living bread?
pm.resp: Let all the earth cry out to God with joy. Alleluia.
interc: For catechists, teachers of Scripture and all who sit beside seekers to explain the faith.
For the Christians of Africa, and for the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, that we may grow in unity.
For those who feel excluded from the people of God, that they may find a welcome.
For the newly baptized, that they may go on their way rejoicing.
For our group, that our hunger for the living bread may grow.
pm.close: Father, you draw all people to your Son. Make us patient guides and joyful witnesses, and feed us with the bread of eternal life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: On the road to Damascus the risen Jesus stopped Saul: I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
Ananias, though afraid, laid hands on him and called him brother; Saul was baptized and proclaimed Jesus.
Jesus said: my flesh is true food and my blood is true drink; whoever eats it abides in me.
2027-04-16.action: Be kind today to someone you have avoided, and call them by name.
2027-04-16.question: Do I treat Christ's body, the Church and the poor, as I would treat Christ himself?

family.explain: Saul did not like Christians and wanted to put them in prison. On the way to Damascus a bright light shone and Jesus spoke to him: Saul, why are you hurting me? Saul was blind for three days. Then a man named Ananias came, put his hands on him and said: Brother Saul. Saul could see again, was baptized and became the great St Paul!
family.intention: We pray for people who are against God and the Church, that Jesus may meet them as he met Saul.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone I do not like? Can I be kind to them tomorrow, like Ananias?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Thodupuzha a young man joined a gang that harassed the parish youth after their evening prayer meetings. One night he broke the windows of the parish hall. The youth group leader, a girl who taught in the Sunday school, found out who it was. Instead of going to the police, she went to his house with the parish priest and said only: we need help to fix the windows before Sunday. Will you come? He came, out of shame. He stayed for the prayer that evening. Years later he became the president of that same youth group.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, true food and true drink, open our eyes as you opened the eyes of Saul, and let us abide in you. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? (Acts 9:4). How do I wound Christ when I wound his people?
Brother Saul (Acts 9:17). Whom do I find it hard to call brother or sister?
My flesh is true food and my blood is true drink (John 6:55). Do I receive Holy Communion as true food, with faith and wonder?
pm.resp: Go out to all the world and tell the Good News. Alleluia.
interc: For those who persecute Christians, that the risen Lord may meet them as he met Saul.
For all who are called, like Ananias, to welcome converts and returning sinners.
For a deeper faith in the Real Presence of Christ in the Eucharist throughout our parish.
For the poor and suffering, in whom Christ asks to be served.
For our group, that we may abide in him and he in us.
pm.close: Father, through your Son you make persecutors into apostles. Feed us with his Body and Blood and send us to tell the Good News to all the world. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Church had peace and grew; Peter healed the paralyzed Aeneas in the name of Jesus Christ.
In Joppa Peter raised Tabitha, a woman known for her good works and charity.
When many disciples left Jesus, Peter said: Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.
2027-04-17.action: Do one hidden work of charity with your hands this week.
2027-04-17.question: When a teaching of Jesus is hard for me, do I walk away or stay and ask?

family.explain: Tabitha was a kind lady who sewed clothes for poor widows. When she died, everyone cried and showed Peter the clothes she had made. Peter knelt and prayed, then said: Tabitha, get up! And she opened her eyes and sat up! Jesus gave her life again through Peter's prayer.
family.intention: We pray for all who care for the poor with their hands.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family make or do with our hands this week for someone in need?”

illus: An illustration

When an old widow died in a parish near Kottayam, the family was surprised at the crowd that came to the funeral. Women from the colony near the railway line, an auto driver, two nuns from an orphanage. One by one they told the family what she had done: school uniforms stitched every June, payasam sent on every feast day, a bag of rice left quietly at a door. The orphanage sisters brought a small sweater she had knitted for each child every winter. Her son, who lived abroad, said later: I knew my mother prayed. I did not know she had been a whole parish by herself.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Holy One of God, you have the words of eternal life. Keep us close to you when others turn away. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you (Acts 9:34). Do I give Jesus the credit for the good I do?
She was devoted to good works and acts of charity (Acts 9:36). What will people remember of my hands?
Lord, to whom can we go? (John 6:68). When have I wanted to leave, and what made me stay?
pm.resp: How shall I make a return to the Lord for all the good he has done for me? Alleluia.
interc: For the Church, that she may have peace and be built up in the comfort of the Holy Spirit.
For the sick and paralyzed, and for those who care for them day after day.
For widows and for all who, like Tabitha, serve the poor with their hands.
For those who have turned away from the Church because of a hard teaching, that they may hear Jesus' question again.
For our group, that with Peter we may say: Lord, to whom can we go?
pm.close: Father, your Son has the words of eternal life. Give us the Spirit who gives life, so that we may never turn back from him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Peter explained step by step how God gave the Holy Spirit to the Gentiles.
Who was I that I could hinder God? The Church opened its door to all nations.
Jesus is the gate of the sheep; he gives life in abundance.
2027-04-19.action: Greet or pray today for someone you usually keep outside your circle.
2027-04-19.question: Which voice am I following most these days, and is it the voice of the Shepherd?
catechism: Christ, the one door of the sheepfold.
The Church sent to the whole human race.
The gift of the Spirit after Baptism, from the apostles onward.
kidsaint: Cornelius the centurion

Cornelius was a Roman army officer who prayed every day and gave money to the poor. An angel told him to send for Peter. When Peter came and spoke about Jesus, the Holy Spirit filled Cornelius and his whole family, and they were baptized. Lesson: God loves people of every country and calls everyone to his family.
2027-04-19.special: Easter weekday: Regina Caeli at noon; Alleluia in the antiphons; the paschal candle is lit at Mass.
term: Gentiles

From the Latin gentes, “the nations”: in the Bible, all peoples other than Israel. The Church of Jews and Gentiles together is the first fruit of the Gospel's catholicity, its openness to every people.

family.explain: In Jesus' time, shepherds kept their sheep in a fold with one gate. In the morning the shepherd called, and his sheep came to him because they knew his voice. Jesus says: I am the gate, and I am the shepherd. He knows each of us by name, and he wants us to have a full and happy life with him.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel left out, that they may find a welcome in our family and our parish.
family.ask: Ask: “How do we hear Jesus' voice in our home?” Choose one way to listen to him this week, such as reading the Sunday Gospel together.

illus: An illustration

In a fishing village near Vizhinjam a parish catechism teacher noticed a migrant boy from Odisha standing every Sunday outside the church gate while his father worked. She invited him in; some parents grumbled that he did not know Malayalam. She did not argue. She simply asked the boy to sing a hymn in his own language at the parish feast. When the children heard him sing Alleluia in Odia, the grumbling stopped. A year later the boy made his First Holy Communion with the others, and his father stood at the back, weeping.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, call us by name and lead us out to the pasture of your word. Alleluia. Amen.
share: What God has made clean, you must not call profane (Acts 11:9). Whom do I find it hard to accept?
Who was I that I could hinder God? (Acts 11:17). Where might I be standing in the way of God's work?
I came that they may have life, and have it abundantly (John 10:10). What is stealing life from me, and what is Jesus offering instead?
pm.resp: My soul thirsts for God, for the living God.
interc: For the Church, that her doors may stay open to every people and culture.
For the Holy Father and the bishops, that they may listen to the Spirit as Peter did.
For migrants and strangers in our towns, that they may find a welcome in our parishes.
For those who have stopped listening to the Shepherd's voice, that he may call them back by name.
For our group, that we may explain our faith gently and step by step.
pm.close: Father, you poured out your Spirit on the Gentiles and opened the gate of life to all. Keep us close to Christ, the gate and the Shepherd. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The scattered believers proclaimed Jesus to the Gentiles of Antioch.
Barnabas saw God's grace and rejoiced; at Antioch the disciples were first called Christians.
Jesus: My sheep hear my voice; no one will snatch them out of my hand; the Father and I are one.
2027-04-20.action: Encourage one person today by naming something good God is doing through them.
2027-04-20.question: If my neighbours had to give me a name from the way I live, would they call me a Christian?
catechism: The Trinity is one God in three persons.
The Son consubstantial with the Father.
“Christian” means anointed, from the name of Christ.
kidsaint: St Barnabas

Barnabas's name means “son of encouragement.” When everybody was afraid of Saul, who used to hurt Christians, Barnabas became his friend and brought him to Antioch. Together they taught many people about Jesus. Lesson: we can be like Barnabas when we encourage others and help them feel welcome.
2027-04-20.special: Easter weekday: Regina Caeli at noon; Alleluia in the antiphons.
term: Consubstantial

From the Latin consubstantialis, translating the Greek homoousios, “of the same substance” or “one in being.” The Creed says the Son is consubstantial with the Father: not a creature, but God from God, light from light.

family.explain: Jesus says his sheep know his voice and follow him. He gives them life that never ends, and he holds them so tightly in his hand that nobody can take them away. And his hand is the same as the Father's hand, because Jesus and the Father are one.
family.intention: We pray for all who are afraid or in danger, that they may feel safe in Jesus' hand.
family.ask: Ask: “What does it mean that our family's name is ‘Christian’?” Make the Sign of the Cross together slowly, remembering whose people we are.

illus: An illustration

A young nurse from Kottayam went to work in a hospital in Riyadh, where there was no parish she could visit openly. At first she felt she had left the Church behind. Then she began to pray the Rosary each night with two Filipino nurses and a Kenyan cleaner in her building. A year later there were fourteen of them, quietly reading the Sunday Gospel together. When she came home on leave, she told her parish priest: I thought I was scattered, but I was being sown.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, we hear your voice; hold us in your hand and send us out to speak your name. Alleluia. Amen.
share: The hand of the Lord was with them (Acts 11:21). Where have I seen God's hand in the spread of the faith?
When he came and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced (Acts 11:23). Whose good work can I rejoice in and encourage?
No one will snatch them out of my hand (John 10:28). What fear do I need to place in the hand of Jesus?
pm.resp: All you nations, praise the Lord.
interc: For Christians scattered by work, migration or persecution, that they may be seeds of the Gospel wherever they live.
For the persecuted Church, that the Lord may hold her in his hand.
For pastors and leaders, that like Barnabas they may see grace and encourage it.
For our Jewish brothers and sisters, the first to hear the word of God, that they may be blessed in faithfulness to his covenant.
For our group, that we may truly deserve the name Christian.
pm.close: Father, your Son holds his sheep in your hand. Keep us faithful to him and make us bearers of his name to all peoples. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: At Antioch, during worship and fasting, the Holy Spirit set apart Barnabas and Saul for mission.
Jesus: I have come as light into the world; whoever sees me sees him who sent me.
St Anselm: faith seeking understanding.
2027-04-21.action: Pray today for one missionary by name, and if you can, send them a word of support.
2027-04-21.question: Do I try to understand my faith better, or am I content to know only what I learned as a child?
catechism: The Holy Spirit, protagonist of mission.
kidsaint: St Anselm

Anselm grew up in the mountains of Italy and dreamed that God lived on the top of the highest peak. When he grew up he became a monk and spent his life thinking and praying about God. He became the Archbishop of Canterbury in England and was brave when the king tried to boss the Church. Lesson: we can use our minds to love God more, by learning about him and praying.
2027-04-21.special: Optional memorial of St Anselm: white vestments; the Easter weekday readings; Regina Caeli at noon.
term: Faith seeking understanding

In Latin fides quaerens intellectum, the phrase of St Anselm. Faith is not blind; the believer, already trusting God, uses the mind to understand more deeply what God has revealed. This is the task of theology (Catechism 158).

family.explain: In the church at Antioch the leaders were praying and fasting together. The Holy Spirit told them: choose Barnabas and Saul for a special work. So they prayed again, laid their hands on them, and sent them off to tell other countries about Jesus. That was the beginning of St Paul's great journeys.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries all over the world, especially those from our own parish and diocese.
family.ask: Ask: “What job might God be choosing each of us for?” Before the next family decision, decide to pray about it together first.

illus: An illustration

A retired engineer in Thrissur, a daily communicant, kept a notebook of questions his grandson asked him about God: why does God allow suffering, how can bread become Jesus, how can three be one. He did not want to give lazy answers. So each evening, after the Rosary, he read a page of the Catechism and a page of the Fathers, and wrote down what he learned. After three years the notebook had become a small handwritten book. His grandson, now at a seminary, keeps it on his desk. On the first page the old man had written: I believe, so that I may understand.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, you set apart Barnabas and Saul during prayer. Speak to us now as we worship and listen. Alleluia. Amen.
share: While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul (Acts 13:2). What is the Spirit asking of me?
Whoever sees me sees him who sent me (John 12:45). How has Jesus shown me the face of the Father?
I have come as light into the world (John 12:46). What darkness in my life needs his light?
pm.resp: O God, let all the nations praise you!
interc: For missionaries of our diocese and parish, that the Spirit may sustain them.
For those discerning a call to priesthood or religious life, that they may hear the Spirit's voice in prayer.
For theologians and teachers of the faith, that like St Anselm they may join study to prayer.
For those who live in darkness, that the light of Christ may reach them.
For our group, that we may pray and fast before every important decision.
pm.close: Father, through St Anselm you taught your Church to seek understanding in faith. Grant that we may believe more deeply, understand more clearly and love more ardently. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: John Mark turned back, but later Paul called him useful: God gives second chances.
Paul preached in the synagogue God's faithfulness to Israel, fulfilled in Jesus, son of David.
Jesus: servants are not greater than their master; whoever receives my messenger receives me.
2027-04-22.action: Do one hidden act of service today that no one will thank you for.
2027-04-22.question: Is there someone I have refused to give a second chance?
catechism: The apostles, sent as Christ was sent.
John the Baptist, precursor of the Lord.
kidsaint: St John the Baptist

John the Baptist was a great prophet. Huge crowds came to hear him by the river Jordan. Some people even thought he was the Messiah. But John said: I am not even good enough to untie his sandals! He pointed everyone to Jesus. Lesson: being humble means we point to Jesus, not to ourselves.
2027-04-22.special: Easter weekday: Regina Caeli at noon; Alleluia in the antiphons.
term: Synagogue

From the Greek for “gathering.” The Jewish house of prayer and study, where the Law and Prophets were read every sabbath. The Christian Liturgy of the Word grew from this tradition of reading and explaining the Scriptures.

family.explain: At the Last Supper Jesus, the Lord and Teacher, knelt down and washed his friends' feet. Then he said: a servant is not greater than his master. If I have washed your feet, you should wash one another's feet. You will be happy if you do it.
family.intention: We pray for all who serve others quietly: mothers and fathers, nurses, cleaners, and all who work without thanks.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one ‘foot-washing job’ each of us can do for the family this week?” Choose one and do it without being asked.

illus: An illustration

A young man from Alappuzha left the seminary in his second year, ashamed and confused. For a long time he avoided the priests who had taught him. Years later, married and working as a teacher, he received a phone call from the old rector: our parish youth have no one to guide them; you were always good with young people. Will you help? He hesitated, then said yes. Today he leads the diocesan youth movement. He says: I thought my turning back was the end of my story. God thought it was a chapter.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you washed the feet of your disciples. Make us humble servants and faithful messengers. Alleluia. Amen.
share: John, however, left them and returned to Jerusalem (Acts 13:13). Where have I turned back, and how is God calling me again?
Of this man's posterity God has brought to Israel a Savior, Jesus, as he promised (Acts 13:23). How has God kept his promises in my life?
Servants are not greater than their master (John 13:16). What humble service is Jesus asking of me?
pm.resp: For ever I will sing the goodness of the Lord.
interc: For all who have turned back from their vocation or their faith, that God may give them a second chance.
For our Jewish brothers and sisters, heirs of the promises to Abraham and David.
For priests and all who serve in the Church, that they may be humble servants like their Master.
For those who serve without recognition, that the Lord may reward them.
For our group, that we may receive every messenger of Christ with faith.
pm.close: Father, you are faithful to every generation. Make us humble servants of your Son and messengers of his love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul preached: God raised Jesus from the dead and fulfilled his promise; you are my Son.
Jesus: Do not let your hearts be troubled; in my Father's house there are many dwelling places.
I am the way, and the truth, and the life: St George and St Adalbert followed him to martyrdom.
2027-04-23.action: Pray today for one Christian community that is persecuted for its faith.
2027-04-23.question: What is troubling my heart, and have I truly given it to Jesus?
kidsaint: St George

George was a brave soldier who loved Jesus. When the emperor ordered everyone to worship false gods, George said no, because he belonged to Jesus. He was killed for his faith. Later people told a story about George fighting a dragon, to show that with Jesus we can defeat evil. Lesson: we can be brave and say no to what is wrong, because Jesus is with us.
2027-04-23.special: Optional memorials of St George and St Adalbert: red vestments if one is kept; the Easter weekday readings; Regina Caeli at noon.
term: Martyr

From the Greek martys, “witness.” A martyr is one who bears witness to Christ even unto death. The Church honours martyrs from the beginning: their feast is their “birthday” into heaven (dies natalis).

family.explain: At the Last Supper the disciples were afraid because Jesus was going away. He told them: do not be worried. My Father's house has many rooms, and I am going to get a place ready for you. Then I will come back and take you with me. Thomas asked: how can we know the way? Jesus said: I am the way.
family.intention: We pray for those who are afraid of dying, and for our family members who have died, that they may be at home in the Father's house.
family.ask: Ask: “What do you think heaven is like?” Talk about it together, and remember that heaven means being with Jesus.

illus: An illustration

Every year on the feast of St George an old woman from a village near Kollam walked many kilometres to the church dedicated to him, carrying a small offering in a cloth. Her grandson, an engineering student, laughed at her: Ammachi, do you really believe in dragons? She smiled and said: I don't come for a dragon. I come because a soldier gave his life rather than deny Jesus. When I am afraid, I remember him, and I am not afraid any more. Years later, when that grandson faced pressure at work to sign a false report, he remembered her words and refused.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the way, the truth and the life. Calm our troubled hearts and lead us to the Father's house. Alleluia. Amen.
share: But God raised him from the dead (Acts 13:30). How does the Resurrection change the way I face injustice?
Do not let your hearts be troubled (John 14:1). What fear do I bring to Jesus tonight?
I am the way, and the truth, and the life (John 14:6). Where am I tempted to look for another way?
pm.resp: You are my Son; this day I have begotten you.
interc: For the persecuted Church, that like St George and St Adalbert her members may remain faithful.
For soldiers, police and all who serve in uniform, that they may protect life and act justly, under the patronage of St George.
For the peoples of Poland and the Czech lands, and for missionaries among peoples who do not yet know Christ.
For the dying, that Jesus may take them to himself in the Father's house.
For our group, that our hearts may not be troubled but firm in faith.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son and made him the way to you. By the prayers of your martyrs St George and St Adalbert, keep us faithful to him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul and Barnabas, rejected by some, turned to the Gentiles: a light for the nations.
Driven out of the city, the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
Jesus: Whoever has seen me has seen the Father; ask in my name and I will do it.
2027-04-24.action: Ask Jesus today for one big intention, explicitly in his name.
2027-04-24.question: Do I look for God somewhere else, when he has shown his face in Jesus?
catechism: Prayer in the name of Jesus.
The Church and the Jewish people.
kidsaint: St Fidelis of Sigmaringen

Fidelis was a clever lawyer who helped poor people without asking for money. But he wanted to give everything to God, so he became a Capuchin friar with a long beard and a rough brown habit. He visited the sick, prayed for hours before Jesus in the tabernacle, and went to preach in Switzerland, where he was killed for his faith. His name means “faithful.” Lesson: we can be faithful to Jesus every day, in small things and big ones.
2027-04-24.special: Optional memorial of St Fidelis: red vestments if kept; the Easter weekday readings; Regina Caeli at noon.
term: Propaganda Fide

The Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith, founded by Pope Gregory XV in 1622 to direct the missions of the Church. Since 2022 its work continues in the Dicastery for Evangelization. Many dioceses of India were founded under its care.

family.explain: Philip, one of Jesus' friends, said: Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us. Jesus said: Philip, you have been with me so long! Whoever has seen me has seen the Father. When we look at Jesus, how kind and loving he is, we see what God the Father is like.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries who are not welcomed, that they may keep their joy.
family.ask: Ask: “What does Jesus show us about God the Father?” Let each person name one thing, such as kindness, forgiveness or patience.

illus: An illustration

A young woman catechist from Kannur volunteered with a mission in a tribal area of Jharkhand. In one village the headman refused to let her teach and told her to leave. She was hurt, but she remembered the words of Acts: they shook the dust off their feet, and were filled with joy. She went to the next village, singing on the bus. A year later the headman's daughter came to her class there, and later the headman himself asked her to start a school in his village. She says: rejection was not the end of the road; it was just a turn.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, show us the Father. Fill us with joy and with the Holy Spirit, even when we are not welcomed. Alleluia. Amen.
share: I have set you to be a light for the Gentiles (Acts 13:47). To whom is the Lord sending me as a light?
The disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit (Acts 13:52). How can I keep my joy when I am rejected?
Whoever has seen me has seen the Father (John 14:9). What have I seen of the Father in Jesus?
pm.resp: All the ends of the earth have seen the saving power of God.
interc: For missionaries who face rejection, that they may be filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
For the Jewish people, to whom the word of God was first spoken, that God may bless them.
For Christian unity, that Catholics and Protestants may walk together in truth and charity.
For lawyers and judges, that like St Fidelis they may defend the poor and serve justice honestly.
For our group, that we may ask the Father in the name of Jesus with faith.
pm.close: Father, in your Son we see your face. Fill us with the Holy Spirit and make us faithful witnesses to the ends of the earth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: At Lystra Paul healed a man crippled from birth, and the crowd tried to worship Paul and Barnabas as gods.
The apostles refused: we are mortals like you; turn to the living God who gives rain and joy.
Jesus promises that the Father and the Son will make their home in those who love him, and the Spirit will teach them.
2027-04-26.action: Each time you are thanked or praised today, pass it on to God with a silent “Glory to you, Lord.”
2027-04-26.question: Is my heart a home where the Father and the Son are welcome to stay?

family.explain: When Paul healed a man who could not walk, people thought Paul was a god and wanted to offer him a sacrifice. Paul said: no! I am a person like you. Thank the real God, who sends rain and food and joy. Jesus tells us that if we love him, God comes to live in our hearts, like a guest who stays.
family.intention: We pray for farmers waiting for the monsoon rains, and for everyone who has no food on the table.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make our heart, and our home, a nice place for Jesus to stay?”

illus: An illustration

St Teresa of Kolkata was often praised as a living saint. She used to answer (in substance): I am only a little pencil in the hand of God; he does the writing. Nobody admires a pencil, she would say, only what is written. Like Paul and Barnabas at Lystra, she turned every garland back towards God.

pm.open: Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory. Come and make your home in us. Amen.
share: We are mortals just like you (Acts 14:15). How do I handle praise, and do I let it point to God?
He has not left himself without a witness in doing good (Acts 14:17). Where did I see God's goodness in creation this week?
We will come to them and make our home with them (John 14:23). What would change if I really believed God lives in me?
pm.resp: Not to us, O Lord, but to your name give the glory.
interc: For missionaries who bring the Gospel to people who have never heard it, that they may speak with humility and joy.
For all who are disabled from birth, and for their families and carers.
For farmers and for good rains in the coming monsoon.
For leaders and celebrities who are flattered and praised, that they may not take God's place.
For our group, that the Holy Spirit may teach us and remind us of the words of Jesus.
pm.close: Father, with your Son you come to dwell in those who love you. Keep our hearts open to you, through the Holy Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: At Lystra Paul was stoned and left for dead, but he got up and went back into the city.
Paul and Barnabas returned to strengthen the new Christians, appointed elders and entrusted them to the Lord with prayer and fasting.
Jesus gives a peace that is not like the world's peace: it can live in a heart surrounded by trouble.
2027-04-27.action: Exchange the sign of peace today with real attention, or make peace with someone at home.
2027-04-27.question: Do I look for peace in having no problems, or in the presence of Christ with me in my problems?

family.explain: Some people threw stones at Paul until he fell down, and they thought he was dead. His friends gathered round him, and he got up and kept going! Jesus said to his friends: I give you my peace. His peace is not only for when everything is nice. It is for when things are hard too.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who are hurt or chased away because they believe in Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “When did our family feel Jesus' peace even when something was going wrong?”

illus: An illustration

Cardinal Francis Xavier Nguyen Van Thuan was arrested in Vietnam in 1975 and spent thirteen years in prison, nine of them in solitary confinement. He later told how friends smuggled in a little wine, labelled as medicine for his stomach, and how he celebrated Mass each day with three drops of wine and one drop of water in the palm of his hand. Guards who had been ordered to guard him came, in time, to respect and even love him. His peace did not come from the prison; it came from the One he held in his hand.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you leave us your peace. Calm our troubled hearts and make us people of peace. Amen.
share: When the disciples surrounded him, he got up and went into the city (Acts 14:20). After a fall, who helps me to get up, and whom do I help?
It is through many persecutions that we must enter the kingdom of God (Acts 14:22). How do I respond when following Jesus costs me something?
I do not give to you as the world gives (John 14:27). Where do I usually look for peace?
pm.resp: Your friends make known, O Lord, the glorious splendour of your kingdom.
interc: For Christians who are persecuted, imprisoned or driven from their homes, that the peace of Christ may guard their hearts.
For bishops, priests and parish leaders, entrusted to the Lord with prayer as the first elders were.
For all who are discouraged after failure or injury, that they may rise again.
For peace in places of war and violence, and for those who work for reconciliation.
For our group, that we may be bearers of Christ's peace in our homes.
pm.close: Father, your Son gave his peace to the apostles on the night before he died. Let that peace keep our hearts and minds in him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: In Antioch some believers taught that Gentile converts must be circumcised to be saved, and a sharp debate began.
Instead of dividing, the Church sent Paul and Barnabas to Jerusalem to the apostles and elders, who met to consider the question.
Jesus is the vine and we are the branches; the Father prunes us so that we bear more fruit. St Peter Chanel and St Louis de Montfort bore fruit after their deaths.
2027-04-28.action: Pray today for unity among Christians, and for one person you disagree with.
2027-04-28.question: When I disagree with someone in the Church, do I seek communion or do I walk away?
kidsaint: St Peter Chanel

A French priest who sailed across the ocean to a tiny island called Futuna. He learned the people's language and looked after the sick so kindly that they called him the man with the good heart. Some people did not want him there, and he was killed. Soon afterwards almost everyone on the island became a Christian. Lesson: love is never wasted, even when we cannot see the fruit yet.

family.explain: Long ago the first Christians had a big argument. They did not split up. They went to Jerusalem to ask the apostles, Peter and the others, and they prayed and talked it through together. Jesus says: I am the vine, you are the branches. A branch that stays on the plant has fruit; a branch that falls off dries up.
family.intention: We pray for Christians in Oceania and the Pacific islands, through St Peter Chanel, and for families where there are quarrels.
family.ask: Ask: “When we argue at home, how can we solve it like the first Christians did?”

illus: An illustration

St Peter Chanel arrived on the small Pacific island of Futuna in 1837. He learned the language, cared for the sick, and was called by the islanders the man with the good heart, yet in more than three years only a handful asked for baptism. When the son of the island's ruler wished to become a Christian, the ruler's anger turned on the missionary, and on 28 April 1841 Peter was clubbed to death. Within a few years almost the whole island had become Catholic. The pruning had been severe; the fruit came after him.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, true vine, keep us joined to you and to one another. Amen.
share: After Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and debate with them (Acts 15:2). How do I behave in a disagreement?
They reported the conversion of the Gentiles, and brought great joy to all the believers (Acts 15:3). Do I rejoice when others come to faith, even if they are different from me?
Every branch that bears fruit he prunes to make it bear more fruit (John 15:2). What pruning is God doing in my life?
pm.resp: Let us go rejoicing to the house of the Lord.
interc: For the unity of the Church, and for all Christian communities divided by disputes.
For the Pope and the bishops, successors of the apostles, that the Spirit may guide their decisions.
For the Church in Oceania and for missionaries in difficult places, through St Peter Chanel.
For all who consecrate themselves to Jesus through Mary, through St Louis de Montfort.
For our group, that we may abide in Christ and bear fruit that lasts.
pm.close: Father, you prune the branches so that they may bear more fruit. Keep us in your Son and in the communion of his Church. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: At the council in Jerusalem Peter declared that Jews and Gentiles alike are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus.
James confirmed it, and the Church decided not to burden Gentile believers with the whole Law of Moses.
Jesus asks us to abide in his love so that his joy may be in us; St Catherine of Siena lived that love with fire.
2027-04-29.action: Pray today for the Pope and for the unity of the Church, as St Catherine did all her life.
2027-04-29.question: Do I live my faith as a set of rules to carry, or as a love to abide in?
kidsaint: St Catherine of Siena

Catherine grew up in a big family in Siena, Italy; she had more than twenty brothers and sisters! She loved Jesus so much that she spent hours praying, and then went out to look after the sick and the poor. She was not afraid to talk even to the Pope and tell him what God wanted. Lesson: love Jesus with all your heart and speak the truth kindly and bravely.

family.explain: The first Christians decided together that everyone, from every country, is saved by the love and grace of Jesus, not by keeping a long list of rules. Jesus says: I love you as my Father loves me. Stay in my love, and you will have my joy. St Catherine stayed so close to Jesus that her joy and love were like a fire.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope, for Italy and Europe, and for everyone who works to make peace.
family.ask: Ask: “What makes us feel that Jesus loves us?”

illus: An illustration

In 1376 Catherine, a dyer's daughter from Siena, travelled to Avignon in France, where the popes had lived for nearly seventy years. She had already written to Pope Gregory XI, calling him her sweet Christ on earth and begging him with great respect and great boldness to come back to Rome. Many cardinals opposed it. In January 1377 the Pope entered Rome. A young woman with no title or office had spoken truth to the highest authority on earth, not out of pride, but out of love for the Church.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you love us as the Father loves you. Keep us in your love and fill us with your joy. Amen.
share: We believe that we will be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they will (Acts 15:11). Do I try to earn God's love?
We should not trouble those Gentiles who are turning to God (Acts 15:19). Do I put unnecessary burdens on others who are coming to faith?
So that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be complete (John 15:11). What steals my joy, and how can I abide in his love?
pm.resp: Proclaim his marvellous deeds to all the nations.
interc: For the Pope, that he may be strengthened by the prayers of the faithful as St Catherine strengthened the popes of her day.
For the unity of the Church, and for all who work to heal divisions.
For Italy and Europe, under the patronage of St Catherine, that they may rediscover their Christian roots.
For women who serve the Church with wisdom and courage, and for all lay Dominicans.
For our group, that we may abide in the love of Jesus and share his joy.
pm.close: Father, you made St Catherine burn with love for your Son and his Church. Through her prayers, keep us in his love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The apostles and elders sent a letter to Antioch: it has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay no further burden on you than the essentials.
The believers in Antioch read it and rejoiced.
Jesus calls us friends, chose us, and commands us to love one another as he has loved us. St Pius V handed on the faith of the Church in the Catechism and the Missal.
2027-04-30.action: Read one paragraph of the Catechism today, or pray one decade of the Rosary for the unity of the Church.
2027-04-30.question: Do I live as a servant who fears, or as a friend of Jesus who has been chosen?
kidsaint: St Pius V

When he was a boy he looked after sheep in the hills of northern Italy. He became a Dominican friar, and later the Pope. Even as Pope he lived simply, ate little, visited sick people in hospital and helped the poor. He asked everyone to pray the Rosary. Lesson: even the most important people are called to be humble servants.

family.explain: The apostles wrote a kind letter to the new Christians in Antioch to explain what was really important, and the Christians were very happy when they read it. Jesus says: you are not my servants, you are my friends! And the way to be his friend is to love one another as he loves us.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope and the bishops, that they may teach the faith with love, and for anyone in our family who is far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “What does it mean to be a friend of Jesus? What does a good friend do?”

illus: An illustration

A parish in Thrissur began a small group for young people who had questions about the faith. Instead of arguing, the priest gave each of them a copy of the Youth Catechism and asked them to bring one question every week. One boy said months later: I thought the Church was a list of rules. When I read why, I found it was a letter from a friend. Like the believers in Antioch, he rejoiced at the exhortation.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us friends and chose us. Teach us to love one another as you love us. Amen.
share: It has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us (Acts 15:28). Do I listen to the Holy Spirit through the teaching of the Church?
When its members read it, they rejoiced at the exhortation (Acts 15:31). Does the Gospel bring me joy or only duty?
You did not choose me but I chose you (John 15:16). How does it feel to know that Jesus chose me?
pm.resp: I will give you thanks among the peoples, O Lord.
interc: For the Pope and the bishops, that the Holy Spirit may guide their teaching, as he guided the apostles in Jerusalem.
For catechists and teachers of the faith, through St Pius V.
For all who feel unwanted or unchosen, that they may know they are friends of Jesus.
For the sick in hospitals and those who serve them.
For our group, that we may love one another as Jesus loves us, and prepare well for the month of Mary.
pm.close: Father, your Son laid down his life for his friends. Teach us to love as he loved, and to bear fruit that lasts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, it is evening on the first Easter day, and the disciples are behind locked doors, afraid. Then Jesus comes and stands among them and says: peace be with you (John 20:19). No reproach, no anger, only peace. And he shows them his hands and his side.

Many of us live behind locked doors too: doors of fear, of guilt, of old hurts that we will not let anyone see. The Risen Lord is not stopped by those doors. He comes in, and the first thing he shows us is his wounds, the proof of how much he has loved us.

Then he breathes on them and says: receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them (John 20:22–23). On the very first Easter night Jesus gives his Church the sacrament of mercy. When we go to confession, it is the Risen Lord himself who says through the priest: your sins are forgiven; go in peace.

Thomas was not there, and he would not believe. A week later Jesus comes again, just for him: put your finger here and see my hands. And Thomas cries out: my Lord and my God! (John 20:28). The one who doubted most makes the greatest act of faith. The Lord is patient with our doubts too.

This is why today is called the Sunday of Divine Mercy. Jesus showed St Faustina his Heart, with rays of water and blood flowing out, and asked her to teach the world a simple prayer: Jesus, I trust in you. It is enough to begin there. And mercy, once received, must be shared. The first Christians were of one heart and soul, and there was not a needy person among them (Acts 4:32, 34).

So let us leave this Mass with three things: a heart at peace, because we are forgiven; the words of Thomas on our lips, my Lord and my God; and open hands for the poor. Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe. That blessing is for us. Jesus, I trust in you. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, Thomas said: I will not believe unless I touch Jesus' wounds. Then Jesus came and said: Thomas, come and see! And Thomas said: my Lord and my God!
We cannot see Jesus with our eyes, but we believe in him, and Jesus says we are blessed. Let us say together: Jesus, I trust in you!

intro: The first reading paints a picture of the Easter Church: one heart and soul, powerful testimony, and no one in need. Mercy received in the Upper Room became mercy shared in the community.

sub: A community born of the Resurrection.
The gift of a new heart.
points.apply: Make peace this week with someone in your parish.
Tell one person this week what the risen Lord has done for you.

points.h: Not a needy person among them
points.apply: Make one work of mercy this week for a family in need.

concl: The Easter Church is one in heart, bold in witness and generous to the poor.
Divine Mercy becomes visible when we share it.
opts.resolve: This week I will make peace with one person and do one work of mercy for someone in need.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this Sunday of Divine Mercy the first reading shows us what a community looks like when it has received God's mercy. Now the whole group of those who believed were of one heart and soul (Acts 4:32). These were people who had seen the risen Lord or heard the apostles' witness. The Resurrection did not only change individuals; it created a family.

Ezekiel had promised: I will give them one heart, and put a new spirit within them (Ezekiel 11:19). One heart does not mean everyone is the same. It means that the love of Christ is stronger than our differences. A parish where people of different families, castes, languages and opinions pray and work together is a living sign of the Resurrection. Division, gossip and cold silence are signs that Easter has not yet reached us.

Luke continues: with great power the apostles gave their testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon them all (Acts 4:33). The same men who hid behind locked doors were now speaking boldly. Mercy makes us brave. How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace (Isaiah 52:7). Each of us can tell someone what the Lord has done for us.

And then: there was not a needy person among them (Acts 4:34). The law of Moses had hoped for this: there will, however, be no one in need among you (Deuteronomy 15:4). Those who had land or houses sold them and laid the money at the apostles' feet. The Church does not teach that private property is wrong. But she teaches that the goods of the earth are meant for all, and that the one who has received mercy must show mercy. Jesus told St Faustina that she must show mercy to her neighbours always and everywhere, by deed, by word and by prayer.

So today, let us receive mercy and share it. Make peace with someone. Tell someone about Jesus. Help a family in need. Then our parish will be like the Church of Jerusalem: one heart and soul, full of grace. And at this Mass, let us pray with confidence: Jesus, I trust in you. Alleluia. Amen.

opts.a: Water and blood: the victory of faith
intro: The second reading speaks of the victory that conquers the world, our faith, and of Jesus who came by water and blood. On Divine Mercy Sunday these words shine with special light.

sub: Faith that Jesus is the Christ.
points.apply: Thank God for your Baptism, the day you were born of God.

sub: God's law is not too hard.
points.apply: Keep one commandment you find hard, with joy, this week.
Pray the Chaplet of Divine Mercy this week.

concl: Our faith in the risen Christ is the victory that overcomes the world.
From his pierced side flow the water and blood of mercy.
opts.resolve: This week I will pray the Chaplet of Divine Mercy and keep God's commandments with joy.
homily: Dear friends, St John writes in today's second reading: everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God (1 John 5:1). Faith is not only an opinion. It is a new birth. On the day of our Baptism we were born of God. And John adds that whoever loves the Father loves the child born of him. To be born of God is to belong to a family and to love its members.

Then John says something comforting: for the love of God is this, that we obey his commandments. And his commandments are not burdensome (1 John 5:3).
