while we, for our part, will devote ourselves to prayer and to serving the word.
points.apply: Pray by name for your parish priest and for a deacon you know, and offer to take on one task that frees them for prayer.

points.h: It is I; do not be afraid
sub: Dark, and Jesus not yet come.
q: he made the storm be still, and the waves of the sea were hushed. Then they were glad because they had quiet, and he brought them to their desired haven.
Then they wanted to take him into the boat, and immediately the boat reached the land toward which they were going.
points.apply: Write “It is I; do not be afraid” on a card and keep it where you will see it each morning.

concl: A Church that listens to complaints and cares for the forgotten grows in the word of God.
In every storm, from within or without, the risen Lord comes and says: It is I.
2027-04-10.resolve: Visit or call one lonely elderly person every week of Eastertide.

intro: Theme: “Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life.”
Stephen's shining face, the crowd that wanted only bread, and the one work God asks of us.

sub: The table servant full of the Spirit.
False witnesses, as at the trial of Jesus.
The radiance of one who has been with God.
q: Moses came down from Mount Sinai. As he came down from the mountain with the two tablets of the covenant in his hand, Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God.
And all who sat in the council looked intently at him, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.
points.apply: Before a difficult conversation this week, spend a few minutes with the Lord first, and go in with his peace.

sub: Crossing the lake for more loaves.
The Giver greater than the gift.
q: Why do you spend your money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which does not satisfy? Listen carefully to me, and eat what is good, and delight yourselves in rich food.
Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For it is on him that God the Father has set his seal.
points.apply: Look honestly at how you spend your best hours this week, and give one of them to the food that endures.

sub: Not a list but a person.
Faith as God's work in us.
q: I have chosen the way of faithfulness; I set your ordinances before me.
Jesus answered them, “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.”
points.apply: Begin each morning this week with a simple act of faith: Lord Jesus, I believe in you, whom the Father has sent.

concl: The Spirit made a table servant shine with the peace of the risen Lord.
Jesus calls us beyond the bread that perishes to faith in him, the bread that endures.
2027-04-12.resolve: Make an act of faith every morning this week and one visit to the Blessed Sacrament.

intro: Theme: “I am the bread of life.”
The first martyr's vision and forgiveness, the true bread from heaven, and a pope who hungered for the truth.

sub: Into your hand I commit my spirit.
q: Into your hand I commit my spirit; you have redeemed me, O LORD, faithful God.
“Look,” he said, “I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!”
points.apply: When trouble comes this week, stop for one moment and lift your eyes: Jesus is standing for you.

points.h: Do not hold this sin against them
sub: A prayer learned at the cross.
The young man with the coats.
q: Therefore I will allot him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he poured out himself to death, and was numbered with the transgressors; yet he bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.
Then he knelt down and cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” When he had said this, he died.
points.apply: Pray Stephen's words every day this week for the person you find hardest to forgive.

sub: Sir, give us this bread always.
q: When the Israelites saw it, they said to one another, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, “It is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat.”
I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
points.apply: Prepare for your next Holy Communion by praying the crowd's words: Lord, give us this bread always.

concl: Stephen died seeing Jesus and forgiving his killers, and his prayer won Saul.
The Father gives us his Son as the true bread from heaven; St Martin I lived on that bread when all else was taken from him.
2027-04-13.resolve: Pray Stephen's prayer daily this week for someone who has hurt you.

intro: Theme: “I will raise them up on the last day.”
The scattering that became a sowing, the joy of Samaria, and the Lord who drives no one away.

sub: The word goes into Judea and Samaria.
q: For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater, so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
Now those who were scattered went from place to place, proclaiming the word.
points.apply: Offer to God one painful change in your life this week and ask him to make it fruitful for the Gospel.

q: Make a joyful noise to God, all the earth; sing the glory of his name; give to him glorious praise.
So there was great joy in that city.
points.apply: Bring the joy of Easter to one place this week where there is little joy: a hospital, a lonely home, a tense office.

q: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak
This is indeed the will of my Father, that all who see the Son and believe in him may have eternal life; and I will raise them up on the last day.
points.apply: Invite back, gently and personally, one person who has drifted away from the Church.

concl: God turns the scattering of his people into the spreading of his word and the joy of new cities.
Jesus receives all who come to him and will raise them up on the last day.
2027-04-14.resolve: Pray this week for one person far from home and one person far from the Church, and reach out to each.

intro: Theme: “I am the living bread that came down from heaven.”
A desert road, a seeker who needed a guide, water for Baptism, and the flesh of Christ given for the life of the world.

points.h: How can I, unless someone guides me?
sub: God sends Philip to one man.
Starting from the Scripture, proclaiming Jesus.
q: So they read from the book, from the law of God, with interpretation. They gave the sense, so that the people understood the reading.

So Philip ran up to it and heard him reading the prophet Isaiah. He asked, “Do you understand what you are reading?” He replied, “How can I, unless someone guides me?” And he invited Philip to get in and sit beside him.
points.apply: Choose one person this week with whom you will read and talk over a passage of the Gospel.

sub: The man the law kept outside.
A name better than sons and daughters.
q: Do not let the foreigner joined to the LORD say, “The LORD will surely separate me from his people”; and do not let the eunuch say, “I am just a dry tree.”
As they were going along the road, they came to some water; and the eunuch said, “Look, here is water! What is to prevent me from being baptized?”
points.apply: Ask yourself honestly whom you would rather keep outside the Church, and pray for them by name.

sub: My flesh for the life of the world.
q: He humbled you by letting you hunger, then by feeding you with manna, with which neither you nor your ancestors were acquainted, in order to make you understand that one does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats of this bread will live forever; and the bread that I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.
points.apply: Make a spiritual communion each day this week, especially on days you cannot go to Mass.

concl: God goes out of his way for a single seeker and opens the Scriptures through those who walk beside him.
The Lamb of whom Isaiah spoke is the living bread, his flesh given for the life of the world.
2027-04-15.resolve: Read one Gospel passage this week with someone younger in the faith, and pray for the person who first taught you.

intro: Theme: “Those who eat my flesh and drink my blood abide in me, and I in them.”
The persecutor stopped on the road, the brother who welcomed him, and the true food and true drink of the Eucharist.

points.h: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?
q: Now the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel said, “Speak, for your servant is listening.”
He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” He asked, “Who are you, Lord?” The reply came, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.”
points.apply: Examine your conscience this week: whom in Christ's body have I hurt, and how can I make it right?

q: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “Come closer to me.” And they came closer. He said, “I am your brother, Joseph, whom you sold into Egypt.”

So Ananias went and entered the house. He laid his hands on Saul and said, “Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on your way here, has sent me so that you may regain your sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
points.apply: Welcome warmly one person who is returning to the Church or new to your parish.

sub: How can this man give us his flesh?
He does not soften his words.
q: Come, eat of my bread and drink of the wine I have mixed.
for my flesh is true food and my blood is true drink. Those who eat my flesh and drink my blood abide in me, and I in them.
points.apply: Make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament this week and tell the Lord simply: I believe you are truly here.

concl: The risen Lord stops the persecutor, and a frightened brother welcomes him into the Church.
Christ gives us his true Body and Blood so that we abide in him and become his body for the world.
2027-04-16.resolve: Visit the Blessed Sacrament once this week and greet one person you have avoided as brother or sister.

intro: Theme: “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.”
Healing in the name of Jesus, a life of charity raised up, and the faith that stays when others leave.

sub: A Church at peace and growing.
q: the LORD opens the eyes of the blind. The LORD lifts up those who are bowed down; the LORD loves the righteous.
Peter said to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you; get up and make your bed!” And immediately he got up.
points.apply: Visit or call one sick or housebound person this week, and pray with them in the name of Jesus.

sub: Devoted to good works and charity.
The Master's words on the disciple's lips.
q: The LORD listened to the voice of Elijah; the life of the child came into him again, and he revived.
Peter put all of them outside, and then he knelt down and prayed. He turned to the body and said, “Tabitha, get up.” Then she opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, she sat up.
points.apply: Make or mend something with your own hands for a poor family or a charitable home this week.

sub: We have come to believe and know.
q: Now if you are unwilling to serve the LORD, choose this day whom you will serve, whether the gods your ancestors served in the region beyond the River or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are living; but as for me and my household, we will serve the LORD.
Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life. We have come to believe and know that you are the Holy One of God.”
points.apply: Renew your faith before the tabernacle this week with Peter's words, especially if something in the faith is hard for you.

concl: The risen Lord heals and raises up through the faith and prayer of his Church.
When the teaching is hard, we stay with Peter, because Jesus alone has the words of eternal life.
2027-04-17.resolve: Do one hidden work of charity this week and pray Peter's words before the tabernacle.

intro: Theme: “I am the gate.”
The vision at Joppa, the Spirit poured out on the Gentiles, and the Shepherd who gives life in abundance.

sub: The sheet let down from heaven.
q: for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
But a second time the voice answered from heaven, ‘What God has made clean, you must not call profane.’
points.apply: When you disagree with someone in the Church this week, tell what you have seen God do, calmly and in order, instead of arguing.

points.h: Who was I to hinder God?
sub: A little Pentecost in a Gentile house.
q: Then afterward I will pour out my spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.
If then God gave them the same gift that he gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I could hinder God?
points.apply: Name one prejudice that keeps you from welcoming someone, and ask the Holy Spirit to remove it.

sub: The fold and its one gate.
q: As a deer longs for flowing streams, so my soul longs for you, O God.
The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I came that they may have life, and have it abundantly.
points.apply: Give the first ten minutes of tomorrow morning to the Shepherd's voice in his word, before any other voice.

concl: The Holy Spirit opened the gate of the Church to every nation, and Peter would not stand in the way.
Christ is the one gate and the Good Shepherd; through him we go in and out and find pasture.
2027-04-19.resolve: This week, welcome one person whom you have kept outside the gate.

intro: Theme: “My sheep hear my voice.”
Scattered believers who sowed the word, Barnabas who rejoiced in grace, and the Shepherd's hand that no one can open.

q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number became believers and turned to the Lord.
points.apply: Wherever you live or work, say one word about Jesus this week to someone who has never heard it from you.

points.h: A good man, full of the Spirit
q: Anxiety weighs down the human heart, but a good word cheers it up.
When he came and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced, and he exhorted them all to remain faithful to the Lord with steadfast devotion;
points.apply: Send a message of encouragement today to someone serving in your parish.

sub: They hear, he knows, they follow.
The Father and I are one.
q: For thus says the Lord God: I myself will search for my sheep, and will seek them out.
My sheep hear my voice. I know them, and they follow me.
points.apply: Each night this week, place your biggest worry in the hand of Jesus with one sentence of trust.

concl: God turned the scattering of his people into the sowing of his word, and at Antioch they were first called Christians.
Christ, one with the Father, holds his sheep so firmly that no one can snatch them from his hand.
2027-04-20.resolve: Live this week so that your name, Christian, is true.

intro: Theme: “I have come as light into the world.”
A mission born in prayer, the light that shows us the Father, and a saint who believed in order to understand.

sub: Hands laid on, sent by the Spirit.
q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”
points.apply: Before your next important decision, give one day to prayer and a small fast, and listen.

sub: To see him is to see the Father.
Not to judge, but to save.
q: For with you is the fountain of life; in your light we see light.
I have come as light into the world, so that everyone who believes in me should not remain in the darkness.
points.apply: Bring one hidden thing into the light this week, in confession or in an honest conversation.

sub: I believe so that I may understand.
q: “Come,” my heart says, “seek his face!” Your face, Lord, do I seek.
Always be ready to make your defense to anyone who demands from you an accounting for the hope that is in you;
points.apply: Choose one article of the Creed and read what the Catechism says about it, beginning and ending with prayer.

concl: The mission of the Church is born in worship and is the work of the Holy Spirit.
Christ is the light in which we see the Father, and like St Anselm we seek to understand what we believe.
2027-04-21.resolve: This week, pray before every important decision and read one page of the Catechism.

intro: Theme: “Whoever receives one whom I send receives me.”
The one who turned back and was restored, God's faithfulness to Israel, and the dignity of humble service.

sub: David, a man after God's heart.
q: I will sing of your steadfast love, O Lord, forever; with my mouth I will proclaim your faithfulness to all generations.
Of this man's posterity God has brought to Israel a Savior, Jesus, as he promised;
points.apply: Write down three promises God has kept in your life and thank him for them tonight.

points.h: Not worthy to untie his sandals
sub: John the Baptist points away from himself.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the Lord require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
Very truly, I tell you, servants are not greater than their master, nor are messengers greater than the one who sent them.
points.apply: Do one lowly task this week that you usually leave to others.

q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace,
Very truly, I tell you, whoever receives one whom I send receives me; and whoever receives me receives him who sent me.
points.apply: Welcome the next priest, catechist or Church visitor to your home as Christ himself.

concl: God keeps faith with Israel and fulfils his promises in Jesus, son of David.
He gives second chances to those who turn back, and he is present in his humble messengers.
2027-04-22.resolve: Give someone a second chance this week, as Paul did with Mark.

intro: Theme: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.”
God's answer to the Cross, the peace Jesus gives to troubled hearts, and two martyrs who walked his way to the end.

q: I will tell of the decree of the Lord: He said to me, “You are my son; today I have begotten you.”
But God raised him from the dead;
points.apply: When you meet injustice this week, pray: Lord, you have the last word, and your word is life.

points.h: Do not let your hearts be troubled
q: do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my victorious right hand.
“Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, believe also in me.”
points.apply: Give your greatest worry to Jesus tonight in a few honest words, and leave it with him.

sub: Not a map, but a person.
q: You show me the path of life. In your presence there is fullness of joy; in your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
points.apply: Pray today for a Christian community that suffers for the faith, and ask the martyrs for courage in your own small trials.

concl: The Resurrection is God's answer to the injustice of the Cross and the fulfilment of his promises.
Christ is the way to the Father's house; the martyrs followed him there, and he calls us to follow.
2027-04-23.resolve: Each evening this week, say: Jesus, you are my way; I trust you.

intro: Theme: “Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.”
A light for the nations, joy in rejection, and the face of the Father in Jesus.

sub: Sent to the ends of the earth.
q: All the ends of the earth have seen the victory of our God.
For so the Lord has commanded us, saying, ‘I have set you to be a light for the Gentiles, so that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’
points.apply: Pray this week for one people or region in India that has not yet heard the Gospel.

q: yet I will rejoice in the Lord; I will exult in the God of my salvation.
And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: When something you do for God is rejected, pray for those who rejected it and refuse to lose your joy.

sub: The face of God in Jesus.
Asking in his name; St Fidelis, faithful to death.
q: Moses said, “Show me your glory, I pray.”
Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.
points.apply: Spend ten minutes this week before the Blessed Sacrament, asking: Lord, show me the Father.

concl: The Church is sent to be a light to the nations, and her joy does not depend on success.
In Jesus we see the Father; like St Fidelis, we are called to be faithful until death.
2027-04-24.resolve: This week, end every petition with “in the name of Jesus,” and keep your joy whatever happens.

intro: Theme: “We will come to them and make our home with them.”
Apostles who refuse worship, a Creator who never leaves himself without witness, and a God who comes to stay.

sub: A witness points away from himself.
q: Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory, for the sake of your steadfast love and your faithfulness.

Friends, why are you doing this? We are mortals just like you, and we bring you good news, that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all that is in them.
points.apply: This week, whenever you succeed or are praised, say aloud or in your heart: not to us, Lord, but to your name.

q: The heavens are telling the glory of God; and the firmament proclaims his handiwork.
Ever since the creation of the world his eternal power and divine nature, invisible though they are, have been understood and seen through the things he has made.
points.apply: Before each meal this week, name one gift of creation on your plate and thank the Creator for it.

points.h: We will make our home with them
sub: Not a visit but a dwelling.
q: My dwelling place shall be with them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
Jesus answered him, “Those who love me will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them.”
points.apply: Each night until Pentecost, end the day with a minute of silence before the God who lives in you, and pray: Come, Holy Spirit.

concl: The apostles at Lystra refused to be gods so that people might find the true God.
That God does not visit and leave: with the Father and the Spirit, the risen Jesus makes his home in those who love him.
2027-04-26.resolve: Pray “Come, Holy Spirit” each evening from now until Pentecost.

intro: Theme: “My peace I give to you.”
Paul rises from the stones, the young churches are strengthened, and Christ gives a peace the world cannot give.

points.h: He got up and went into the city
sub: Praise one day, stones the next.
Back into the city, not away from it.
q: Do not rejoice over me, O my enemy; when I fall, I shall rise; when I sit in darkness, the Lord will be a light to me.
We are afflicted in every way, but not crushed; perplexed, but not driven to despair; persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed;
points.apply: Like the disciples at Lystra, stand beside someone who has been knocked down this week: visit, call or pray with them.

sub: Back to the towns of suffering.
Elders appointed with prayer and fasting.
q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
Look, I have set before you an open door, which no one is able to shut.
points.apply: Pray by name this week for your parish priest and for one missionary you know, entrusting them to the Lord.

sub: Rise, let us be on our way.
q: Those of steadfast mind you keep in peace— in peace because they trust in you.
And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: When anxiety rises this week, stop and pray slowly: Lord Jesus, give me your peace.

concl: Paul rose from the stones and went back to strengthen the churches.
The peace he carried was not the world's calm but the risen Christ's own presence, given to us at every Mass.
2027-04-27.resolve: Make the sign of peace at Mass a real prayer for the person beside you.

intro: Theme: “Apart from me you can do nothing.”
The first dispute of the Church brought to the apostles, the branches joined to the vine, and the Father's pruning; St Peter Chanel and St Louis Grignion de Montfort.

sub: Must a Gentile first become a Jew?
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
making every effort to maintain the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
points.apply: In your next disagreement, listen fully to the other person before you answer.

sub: Not a split but a journey.
q: I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go to the house of the Lord!”
When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth;
points.apply: Pray this week for the Pope and your bishop, and read one short teaching of the Church on a question that troubles you.

sub: Fruit after death: Peter Chanel and Montfort.
q: Blessed are those who trust in the Lord, whose trust is the Lord. They shall be like a tree planted by water, sending out its roots by the stream.
Now, discipline always seems painful rather than pleasant at the time, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
points.apply: Offer one present pain to the Father as pruning, and ask for the fruit he wants, not the fruit you want.

concl: The first Christians met disagreement by going to the apostles and waiting on the Spirit.
The branches stay one by staying on the vine; the Father's pruning, as the saints of today show, brings fruit that outlives us.
2027-04-28.resolve: Make one step of reconciliation this week, and offer one pain to the Father.

intro: Theme: “Abide in my love.”
Salvation by the grace of the Lord Jesus, the Father's love poured out on us, and the fire of St Catherine of Siena.

sub: No distinction between them and us.
A yoke no one could bear.
q: It was not because you were more numerous than any other people that the Lord set his heart on you and chose you—for you were the fewest of all peoples. It was because the Lord loved you and kept the oath that he swore to your ancestors,
For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God
points.apply: Stop trying to earn God's love this week: begin each prayer with thanks for what you have received.

sub: As the Father has loved me.
Commandments as the walls of a home.
q: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you; abide in my love.
points.apply: Choose one commandment you find hard and keep it this week as a way of staying in his love, not as a rule.

sub: Truth spoken to the Pope in love.
q: for love is strong as death, passion fierce as the grave. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a raging flame. Many waters cannot quench love, neither can floods drown it.
“I came to bring fire to the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!”
points.apply: Pray each day this week for the Pope and for one person who has drifted from the Church.

concl: The Church learned at Jerusalem that we are all saved by grace.
That grace is the Father's love for the Son poured into us; St Catherine shows what happens when a heart abides in it: joy, truth and fire.
2027-04-29.resolve: Read a few lines of St Catherine's prayers or letters this week and pray for the Church.

intro: Theme: “You did not choose me but I chose you.”
The Church's letter in the Spirit, the friendship of Jesus, and the commandment of love; St Pius V.

points.h: It has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us
q: The spirit of the Lord shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the Lord.
Now we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit that is from God, so that we may understand the gifts bestowed on us by God.
points.apply: Before Pentecost, read one short document or homily of the Pope, and ask the Spirit to help you receive it with joy.

q: Thus the Lord used to speak to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend.

I do not call you servants any longer, because the servant does not know what the master is doing; but I have called you friends, because I have made known to you everything that I have heard from my Father.
points.apply: Spend ten minutes this week speaking to Jesus as to a friend, telling him plainly what is in your heart.

points.h: Love one another as I have loved you
sub: St Pius V: teaching and service together.
q: You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the Lord.
Beloved, since God loved us so much, we also ought to love one another.
points.apply: Choose one person you find hard to love and do something good for them this week, as Jesus did for you.

concl: The Spirit guided the apostles to hand on the essentials of faith, and the believers rejoiced.
Jesus chose us as friends and sends us to love one another as he loved us; St Pius V shows that clear teaching and humble service belong together.
2027-04-30.resolve: Begin the month of Mary tomorrow by praying the Rosary, or one decade, each day of May.
